title: Ravi's mystery number
statement:
Ravi thinks of a number. He multiplies it by 3 and then adds 7. The result is 40.
What number did Ravi think of?
keySteps: Write the condition as an equation: 3x + 7 = 40.
Undo the addition by subtracting 7 to get 3x = 33.
Undo the multiplication by dividing by 3 to get x = 11.
explanation: Let the number be x, so 3x + 7 = 40. Subtracting 7 gives 3x = 33, and dividing by 3 gives x = 11. Check: 3 × 11 + 7 = 40.
hints: Work backwards from 40.
Before adding 7 the value was 33.
33 was 3 times the number, so divide 33 by 3.

title: Reversed two-digit number
statement:
Sneha writes a two-digit number whose digits add up to 9. When she reverses the digits, the new number is 27 more than the original.
What was the original number?
keySteps: Write the number as 10a + b with a + b = 9.
Reversing gives 10b + a, so (10b + a) − (10a + b) = 9(b − a) = 27.
Solving a + b = 9 and b − a = 3 gives a = 3, b = 6, so the number is 36.
explanation: Let the number be 10a + b. Reversing increases it by 9(b − a) = 27, so b − a = 3. With a + b = 9 we get a = 3 and b = 6, giving 36. Check: 63 − 36 = 27.
hints: Reversing a two-digit number always changes it by 9 times the difference of the digits.
So the digits differ by 27 ÷ 9 = 3.
Find two digits that add to 9 and differ by 3, with the bigger one in the units place.

title: Three consecutive even numbers
statement:
The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 78.
What is the largest of the three numbers?
keySteps: Call the numbers x, x + 2 and x + 4.
explanation: Let the numbers be x, x + 2, x + 4. Then 3x + 6 = 78, so x = 24, and the numbers are 24, 26 and 28. The largest is 28.
hints: The middle number is the average of the three.
78 ÷ 3 = 26 is the middle number.
The largest is 2 more than the middle one.

title: Chairs for the college fest
statement:
For the college fest, Priya must arrange chairs so they can be placed in complete rows of 4, rows of 6 or rows of 9 with none left over.
What is the smallest number of chairs greater than 50 that works?
keySteps: The number must be a common multiple of 4, 6 and 9.
Multiples of 36 are 36, 72, …; the first one above 50 is 72.
explanation: The count must be divisible by 4, 6 and 9, so it is a multiple of LCM(4, 6, 9) = 36. The multiples are 36, 72, 108, …, and the smallest above 50 is 72.
hints: Think about common multiples.
Find the LCM of 4, 6 and 9.
The LCM is 36; which multiple of 36 first exceeds 50?

title: Canteen change
statement:
In the college canteen, Anil buys 3 samosas at ₹15 each and 2 cups of tea at ₹12 each. He pays with a ₹100 note.
How much change, in rupees, should he get back?
keySteps: Total bill is ₹69, so change is 100 − 69 = ₹31.
explanation: Samosas cost 3 × 15 = ₹45 and tea costs 2 × 12 = ₹24, so the bill is ₹69. The change from ₹100 is ₹31.
hints: Find the cost of each item type separately.
The bill is 45 + 24.
Subtract the bill of ₹69 from ₹100.

title: Batting average
statement:
In five innings, Rohit scored 45, 62, 38, 0 and 55 runs. He was out in every innings.
What is his batting average?
keySteps: The duck (0) still counts as an innings.
explanation: The total is 200 runs over 5 completed innings, including the duck. The average is 200 ÷ 5 = 40.
hints: Batting average here is total runs divided by innings.
Do not skip the 0 — it is still an innings.
Total is 200; divide by 5.

title: Auto-rickshaw fare
statement:
An auto-rickshaw in Hyderabad charges ₹30 for the first 2 km and ₹15 for every additional km.
What is the fare, in rupees, for a 9 km ride?
keySteps: The first 2 km cost a flat ₹30.
Extra charge is 7 × 15 = ₹105, so the fare is 30 + 105 = ₹135.
explanation: The first 2 km cost ₹30. The other 7 km cost 7 × ₹15 = ₹105. The total fare is ₹135.
hints: Split the ride into the first 2 km and the rest.
How many km are charged at ₹15?
7 km × ₹15, then add ₹30.

title: Fest ticket sales
statement:
At a college fest, student tickets cost ₹50 and outsider tickets cost ₹80. A total of 120 tickets were sold and ₹7,200 was collected.
How many outsider tickets were sold?
keySteps: If all 120 were student tickets the collection would be 120 × 50 = ₹6,000.
Each outsider ticket adds ₹30 extra, so outsiders = 1200 ÷ 30 = 40.
explanation: Assume all 120 tickets were student tickets: ₹6,000. The extra ₹1,200 comes from outsider tickets, each worth ₹30 more, so there were 1200 ÷ 30 = 40 outsider tickets. Check: 80 × 50 + 40 × 80 = 7,200.
hints: Pretend every ticket was a student ticket first.
That gives ₹6,000, which is ₹1,200 short.
Each outsider ticket adds ₹30 over a student ticket.

title: Hundred days after Monday
statement:
Today is a Monday. Kavya's internship starts exactly 100 days from today.
On which day of the week does her internship start?
keySteps: Days of the week repeat every 7 days.
Two days after Monday is Wednesday.
explanation: After 14 full weeks (98 days) it is Monday again. The remaining 2 days take us to Wednesday.
hints: The week repeats every 7 days.
Find the remainder when 100 is divided by 7.
The remainder is 2; count 2 days on from Monday.

title: Phone on sale
statement:
A phone priced at ₹12,000 is sold with a 15% discount during a Diwali sale.
How much does the buyer pay, in rupees?
keySteps: The discount is subtracted from the marked price.
explanation: The discount is 15% of ₹12,000 = ₹1,800. The buyer pays 12,000 − 1,800 = ₹10,200 (equivalently 85% of 12,000).
hints: Find 10% first, then 5%.
Subtract the 1,800 discount from 12,000.

title: Boys and girls in class
statement:
In a class of 64 students, the ratio of boys to girls is 5 : 3.
How many girls are in the class?
explanation: The ratio 5 : 3 splits the class into 8 equal parts of 8 students each. Girls make up 3 parts, so there are 24 girls.
hints: Add the ratio parts.
Each of the 8 parts is how many students?
Girls are 3 of those parts.

title: Marks to percentage
statement:
Divya scored 72 marks out of 90 in her mid-semester exam.
What is her score as a percentage?
explanation: Her fraction of marks is 72/90 = 4/5 = 0.8, which is 80%.
hints: Write the score as a fraction.
Simplify 72/90.
4/5 as a percentage is …

title: Tea price hike
statement:
The price of a cup of tea at the station stall rose from ₹10 to ₹12.
By what percentage did the price increase?
keySteps: Percentage increase is measured against the original price of ₹10.
explanation: The price went up by ₹2. Compared with the original ₹10, that is 2/10 = 20%.
hints: Find the increase in rupees.
Divide by the old price, not the new one.
2 out of 10 is what percent?

title: Twentieth term
statement:
Look at the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, …
What is its 20th term?
keySteps: The sequence goes up by 4 each time (common difference 4).
explanation: This is an arithmetic sequence with first term 3 and common difference 4. The 20th term is 3 + 19 × 4 = 79.
hints: What is added each time?
From the 1st to the 20th term there are 19 jumps.
Add 19 jumps of 4 to 3.

title: Times-three pattern
statement: Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 6, 18, 54, …
keySteps: Each term divided by the previous term is 3.
So each term is 3 times the one before.
explanation: Each term is multiplied by 3 (2 × 3 = 6, 6 × 3 = 18, 18 × 3 = 54). The next term is 54 × 3 = 162.
hints: Compare each term with the one before it.
Is it adding or multiplying?
Multiply 54 by 3.

title: Missing square
statement: Which number comes next in the sequence 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, … ?
keySteps: The differences 3, 5, 7, 9 increase by 2, confirming the pattern.
explanation: The terms are the perfect squares 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², so the next is 6² = 36. The differences 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 also confirm it.
hints: Look at the differences between terms.
These numbers are special — think of n × n.
5 × 5 = 25, so what is next?

title: Growing daily savings
statement:
Arjun saves ₹10 on day 1, ₹20 on day 2, ₹30 on day 3, and so on, saving ₹10 more each day.
How much, in rupees, has he saved in total after 10 days?
keySteps: On day n he saves 10n rupees, so day 10 is ₹100.
hints: How much does he save on day 10?
Pair the first and last days: 10 + 100, 20 + 90, …
There are 5 pairs of ₹110.

title: Two coins, one head
statement:
Meera tosses two fair coins at the same time.
What is the probability of getting exactly one head? Give your answer as a decimal.
keySteps: List the 4 equally likely outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT.
Exactly one head happens in HT and TH — 2 outcomes.
explanation: The outcomes HH, HT, TH, TT are equally likely. Exactly one head occurs in 2 of them, so the probability is 2/4 = 1/2 = 0.5.
hints: Write out every outcome for two coins.
There are 4 outcomes; which have exactly one H?
Count HT and TH.

title: Red marble from a bag
statement:
A bag has 3 red marbles and 5 blue marbles. Ganesh picks one marble without looking.
What is the probability that it is red? Give your answer as a decimal.
explanation: Each of the 8 marbles is equally likely to be picked and 3 are red, so the probability is 3/8 = 0.375.
hints: Count all the marbles.
Favourable ÷ total.
3 ÷ 8 as a decimal.

title: Laddoo with a cashew
statement:
A box has 20 laddoos that look identical. Only 4 of them have a cashew inside. Lalitha picks one at random.
What is the probability that it has a cashew? Give your answer as a decimal.
explanation: Every laddoo is equally likely to be picked. 4 of the 20 have cashews, so the probability is 4/20 = 1/5 = 0.2.
hints: Favourable ÷ total.
4 out of 20.
Simplify 4/20.

title: Spinner multiple of 3
statement:
A fest game uses a spinner with 10 equal sections numbered 1 to 10.
What is the probability that the spinner stops on a multiple of 3?
keySteps: The multiples of 3 from 1 to 10 are 3, 6 and 9.
explanation: The multiples of 3 between 1 and 10 are 3, 6 and 9 — three of the ten equal sections. The probability is 3/10 = 0.3.
hints: List the multiples of 3 up to 10.
There are three of them.
3 out of 10 sections.

title: Express train speed
statement:
The Godavari Express covers 360 km in 4 hours at a constant speed.
What is its speed in km/h?
keySteps: Distance is 360 km and time is 4 hours.
explanation: Speed is distance divided by time: 360 km ÷ 4 h = 90 km/h.
hints: Recall the formula linking speed, distance and time.
Divide distance by time.

title: Auto ride in minutes
statement:
An auto-rickshaw travels at a steady 30 km/h.
How many minutes does it take to cover 12 km?
explanation: Time = 12 ÷ 30 = 0.4 hours. Converting to minutes, 0.4 × 60 = 24 minutes.
hints: How far does it go in 1 minute?
30 km/h is 0.5 km per minute.
12 ÷ 0.5 minutes.

title: Painting the wall together
statement:
Suresh can paint a wall alone in 6 hours. Mahesh can paint the same wall alone in 3 hours.
Working together, how many hours do they take?
keySteps: Suresh paints 1/6 of the wall per hour.
Mahesh paints 1/3 of the wall per hour.
Together they paint 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 per hour, so they need 2 hours.
explanation: Their hourly rates are 1/6 and 1/3 of the wall. Combined they paint 1/2 of the wall per hour, so the whole wall takes 2 hours.
hints: Think about how much of the wall each paints in one hour.
Add the two hourly fractions.

title: Train passes a pole
statement:
A train 200 m long runs at 72 km/h.
How many seconds does it take to pass a signal pole?
keySteps: To pass a pole the train covers its own length, 200 m.
explanation: The train must travel its own length of 200 m. Its speed is 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s, so it takes 200 ÷ 20 = 10 seconds.
hints: What distance does the train cover while passing a pole?
Convert km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18.
200 m at 20 m/s.

title: Father twice Riya's age
statement:
Riya is 12 years old. Her father is 3 times her age.
In how many years will her father be exactly twice as old as Riya?
explanation: The father is 36. In x years, 36 + x = 2(12 + x) = 24 + 2x, so x = 12. Then Riya is 24 and her father 48.
hints: First find the father's present age.
Add the same number of years to both ages.
Solve 36 + x = 24 + 2x.

title: Arjun and his sister
statement:
The sum of the ages of Arjun and his sister is 30 years. Arjun is 4 years older than his sister.
How old is Arjun?
keySteps: Let the sister be s, so Arjun is s + 4.
explanation: If the sister is s, then 2s + 4 = 30 and s = 13. Arjun is 4 years older, so 17. Check: 17 + 13 = 30.
hints: Write both ages using one unknown.
Remove the 4-year difference first: 30 − 4 = 26.
Split 26 equally, then add 4 back for Arjun.

title: Mother and son five years ago
statement:
The present ages of a mother and her son add up to 50 years. Five years ago, the mother was 7 times as old as her son.
What is the son's present age?
keySteps: Let the son be s now, so the mother is 50 − s.
explanation: With son s and mother 50 − s, five years ago 45 − s = 7(s − 5). So 80 = 8s and s = 10. Check: 5 years ago they were 35 and 5, and 35 = 7 × 5.
hints: Express the mother's age using the son's age.
Subtract 5 from both ages for 'five years ago'.
Solve 45 − s = 7s − 35.

title: Kiran's age riddle
statement:
Six years from now, Kiran's age will be twice what his age was four years ago.
How old is Kiran now?
keySteps: Let the present age be x.
explanation: Let Kiran be x. Then x + 6 = 2(x − 4) = 2x − 8, so x = 14. Check: in 6 years he is 20, and 4 years ago he was 10.
hints: Use one unknown for his present age.
'Six years from now' is x + 6 and 'four years ago' is x − 4.
Solve x + 6 = 2x − 8.

title: Rotis in a hostel mess
statement:
A college hostel mess serves dinner to 300 students. Most students eat around 3 to 5 rotis at dinner.
Roughly how many rotis does the mess make for one dinner?
keySteps: Pick a typical number of rotis per student, about 4.
Multiply by the number of students: 300 × 4 = 1,200.
Check the range: 300 × 3 = 900 and 300 × 5 = 1,500, both inside 800–2,000.
explanation: At about 4 rotis each, 300 students eat roughly 1,200 rotis. Even at the extremes of 3 to 5 rotis the total is 900 to 1,500, which falls in the 800–2,000 range.
hints: Estimate rotis per student.
Multiply by 300.
Try both 3 and 5 rotis to see the range.

title: LCM from product and HCF
statement:
Two numbers have a product of 192 and their HCF is 4.
What is their LCM?
keySteps: For any two numbers, HCF × LCM = product of the numbers.
explanation: Since HCF × LCM equals the product of two numbers, LCM = 192 ÷ 4 = 48. For example, 4 and 48 (or 12 and 16) have product 192, HCF 4 and LCM 48.
hints: There is a standard relation between HCF, LCM and the product.
HCF × LCM = a × b.
Divide 192 by 4.

title: Divisible by 3 or 5
statement: How many whole numbers from 1 to 300 (inclusive) are divisible by 3 or by 5?
keySteps: Numbers divisible by both are multiples of 15: 300 ÷ 15 = 20.
explanation: There are 100 multiples of 3 and 60 multiples of 5, but the 20 multiples of 15 are counted twice. So the answer is 100 + 60 − 20 = 140.
hints: Count multiples of 3 and of 5 separately.
Some numbers were counted twice — which ones?
Subtract the multiples of 15.

title: Factors of 360
statement: How many positive whole-number factors (divisors) does 360 have, including 1 and 360?
keySteps: The number of divisors is the product of (exponent + 1) for each prime.
explanation: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5¹. Each divisor picks a power of 2 (4 ways), of 3 (3 ways) and of 5 (2 ways), giving 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 divisors.
hints: Break 360 into prime factors.
Add 1 to each exponent and multiply.

title: Mix of ₹10 and ₹20 notes
statement:
Meena has ₹500 made up only of ₹10 and ₹20 notes. She has 32 notes in all.
How many ₹20 notes does she have?
keySteps: If all 32 notes were ₹10 notes, the total would be ₹320.
Each ₹20 note adds ₹10 more, so there are 180 ÷ 10 = 18 ₹20 notes.
explanation: Treat all 32 as ₹10 notes: ₹320. The extra ₹180 must come from ₹20 notes, each adding ₹10, so there are 18 of them (and 14 ₹10 notes). Check: 18 × 20 + 14 × 10 = 500.
hints: Assume every note is a ₹10 note.
How far short of ₹500 is that?
Each swap to a ₹20 note adds ₹10.

title: Sixth player's score
statement:
The average score of 5 players in a college cricket team is 48. When a sixth player's score is included, the average becomes 50.
What did the sixth player score?
explanation: The five players scored 240 in total. With six players and average 50 the total is 300, so the sixth player scored 300 − 240 = 60.
hints: Convert averages into totals.
Find both totals.
Subtract the old total from the new total.

title: Markup then discount
statement:
A shopkeeper marks a kurta 40% above its cost price and then gives a 10% discount on the marked price.
What is his profit percentage?
explanation: With cost ₹100, the marked price is ₹140 and the selling price after a 10% discount is ₹126. The profit is ₹26 on ₹100, i.e. 26%.
hints: Assume a convenient cost price like ₹100.
The 10% discount is on the marked price, not the cost.
Selling price is 140 × 0.9.

title: Town population growth
statement:
The population of a town in Andhra Pradesh is 50,000. It grows by 10% every year, each year's growth being on the previous year's population.
What will the population be after 2 years?
keySteps: Growth compounds, so multiply by 1.1 each year.
explanation: Each year the population is multiplied by 1.1. After one year it is 55,000 and after two years 60,500. (It is not 60,000 because the second year's 10% is on 55,000.)
hints: The second year's growth is on the new population.
First year: 55,000.

title: Salary and savings change
statement:
Ramesh spends 60% of his salary and saves the rest. His salary increases by 20% and his spending increases by 10%.
By what percentage do his savings increase?
keySteps: Take the old salary as 100: spending 60, savings 40.
explanation: With a salary of 100, he spends 60 and saves 40. After the changes he earns 120 and spends 66, so he saves 54. The savings rise by 14 on 40, which is 35%.
hints: Use 100 as the old salary.
Work out new salary and new spending separately.
Compare new savings 54 with old savings 40.

title: Double plus one
statement: Find the next number in the sequence: 2, 5, 11, 23, 47, …
explanation: Each term is twice the previous term plus 1 (2→5→11→23→47). So the next term is 2 × 47 + 1 = 95.
hints: Look at the differences.
3, 6, 12, 24 — the next difference is 48.

title: Stadium seating rows
statement:
A college stadium stand has 15 rows. The first row has 20 seats and each row has 3 more seats than the row in front of it.
How many seats are there in total?
keySteps: Seats form an arithmetic series with a = 20, d = 3, n = 15.
explanation: The rows hold 20, 23, …, 62 seats. The sum of the arithmetic series is n(first + last)/2 = 15 × 82 ÷ 2 = 615.
hints: Find the number of seats in the 15th row.
The last row has 20 + 14 × 3 seats.
Use (first + last) × n ÷ 2.

title: Square-number gaps
statement: Find the next number in the sequence: 3, 4, 8, 17, 33, …
keySteps: The next difference is 5² = 25, so the next term is 33 + 25 = 58.
explanation: The gaps 1, 4, 9, 16 are consecutive perfect squares. The next gap is 25, giving 33 + 25 = 58.
hints: Look at the differences between consecutive terms.
1, 4, 9, 16 — recognise them?
Add the next square to 33.

title: Two dice sum to seven
statement:
Two fair dice are rolled together in a board game at the hostel.
What is the probability that the two numbers add up to 7?
explanation: Of the 36 equally likely ordered outcomes, exactly 6 give a sum of 7. So the probability is 6/36 = 1/6.
hints: Count all possible outcomes for two dice.
List ordered pairs that add to 7.
6 favourable out of 36.

title: Two red chits
statement:
A box has 5 chits: 3 red and 2 green. Two chits are drawn together at random.
What is the probability that both are red? Give your answer as a decimal.
keySteps: Number of ways to choose 2 chits from 5 = 5C2 = 10.
Number of ways to choose 2 red chits from 3 = 3C2 = 3.
explanation: There are 5C2 = 10 equally likely pairs, and 3C2 = 3 of them are both red. So the probability is 3/10 = 0.3. (Equivalently 3/5 × 2/4.)
hints: Count all possible pairs of chits.
Count pairs that are both red.
Or multiply 3/5 by 2/4.

title: At least two heads
statement:
A fair coin is tossed 3 times before a gully cricket match.
What is the probability of getting at least 2 heads? Give your answer as a decimal.
keySteps: Exactly 2 heads: 3C2 = 3 outcomes; exactly 3 heads: 1 outcome.
explanation: Of the 8 outcomes, 3 have exactly two heads (HHT, HTH, THH) and 1 has three heads. That is 4/8 = 1/2 = 0.5.
hints: How many outcomes are there for 3 tosses?
'At least 2' means 2 or 3 heads.
Count 3 + 1 favourable outcomes.

title: Trains crossing each other
statement:
Two trains, 150 m and 100 m long, run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 60 km/h and 30 km/h.
How many seconds do they take to cross each other completely?
keySteps: In opposite directions, relative speed = 60 + 30 = 90 km/h.
Distance to cover = sum of lengths = 250 m.
explanation: Moving towards each other, their relative speed is 90 km/h = 25 m/s. To clear each other they must cover 150 + 100 = 250 m, which takes 250 ÷ 25 = 10 seconds.
hints: Opposite directions — add or subtract speeds?
Convert 90 km/h to m/s.
Total distance is both lengths together.

title: A leaves the job midway
statement:
Anand can finish a project in 12 days and Bhavana can finish it in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which Anand leaves.
How many more days does Bhavana need to finish the project alone?
keySteps: In 4 days they finish 4 × 5/36 = 5/9 of the work.
explanation: Together they do 5/36 of the work per day, so 4 days complete 20/36 = 5/9. The remaining 4/9 at Bhavana's rate of 1/18 per day takes 8 days.
hints: Find each person's work per day.
Work done together in 4 days is 4 × (1/12 + 1/18).
Divide the remaining fraction by 1/18.

title: Leaky hostel tank
statement:
A pipe can fill the hostel's overhead tank in 6 hours. A leak at the bottom can empty the full tank in 10 hours.
If the tank starts empty and both work at the same time, how many hours does it take to fill?
keySteps: Pipe fills 1/6 of the tank per hour.
Leak empties 1/10 of the tank per hour.
explanation: The pipe adds 1/6 and the leak removes 1/10 of the tank each hour, a net of 1/15 per hour. So the tank fills in 15 hours.
hints: Write both rates as fractions of the tank per hour.
The leak works against the pipe — subtract.

title: Changing age ratio
statement:
The ages of Anu and Bala are in the ratio 3 : 5. After 8 years, the ratio of their ages will be 5 : 7.
What is Anu's present age?
explanation: With ages 3x and 5x, 7(3x + 8) = 5(5x + 8) gives 4x = 16, so x = 4. Anu is 12 and Bala 20; in 8 years they are 20 and 28, which is 5 : 7.
hints: Write ages as multiples of one unknown.
Add 8 to both and set up the new ratio.
Cross-multiply 7(3x + 8) = 5(5x + 8).

title: Father thrice the son
statement:
A father is now 3 times as old as his son. Ten years ago, the father was 5 times as old as the son.
What is the father's present age?
keySteps: Let the son be s, so the father is 3s.
explanation: With son s and father 3s, ten years ago 3s − 10 = 5(s − 10), so 2s = 40 and s = 20. The father is 60. Check: ten years ago they were 50 and 10.
hints: Use one unknown for the son.
Subtract 10 from both ages.
Solve 3s − 10 = 5s − 50, then multiply by 3.

title: Daily water for a hostel
statement:
A hostel has 200 students. Assume each student uses about as much water per day as a typical Indian city resident (bathing, toilet, washing clothes, drinking).
Roughly how many litres of water does the hostel use in a day?
keySteps: Estimate per-person daily use: roughly 100 to 150 litres (a bucket bath alone is about 20 litres).
Multiply by 200 students: about 20,000 to 30,000 litres.
Choose the range that contains this estimate: 15,000–40,000 litres.
explanation: A city resident uses roughly 100–150 litres a day once bathing, flushing, laundry and drinking are counted. For 200 students that is about 20,000–30,000 litres, which lies in the 15,000–40,000 range. The other options imply under 10 litres or over 2,500 litres per person.
hints: Break a person's day into bathing, toilet, laundry and drinking.
A bucket bath is about 20 litres and each flush about 6–10 litres.
About 120 litres × 200 students.

title: Smallest four-digit remainder puzzle
statement:
When a number is divided by 6, 8 and 10, the remainders are 4, 6 and 8 respectively.
What is the smallest four-digit number with this property?
keySteps: In each case the remainder is 2 less than the divisor.
So the number + 2 is divisible by 6, 8 and 10, i.e. by their LCM 120.
explanation: Each remainder is the divisor minus 2, so N + 2 is a multiple of LCM(6, 8, 10) = 120 and N = 120k − 2. For k = 8, N = 958 (three digits); for k = 9, N = 1078. Check: 1078 leaves remainders 4, 6, 8 on division by 6, 8, 10.
hints: Compare each remainder with its divisor.
Adding 2 makes the number divisible by all three.
Find multiples of 120 just above 1000, then subtract 2.

title: Mixing two teas for profit
statement:
A tea seller mixes tea costing ₹200 per kg with 30 kg of tea costing ₹280 per kg. He sells the mixture at ₹270 per kg and makes a 12.5% profit.
How many kg of the ₹200 tea did he use?
keySteps: Cost price of the mixture = 270 ÷ 1.125 = ₹240 per kg.
So the quantity of ₹200 tea equals the quantity of ₹280 tea, 30 kg.
explanation: A 12.5% profit at ₹270 means the mixture's cost is 270 ÷ 1.125 = ₹240/kg. By alligation the ratio of cheap to costly tea is (280 − 240) : (240 − 200) = 1 : 1, so he used 30 kg of the ₹200 tea. Check: (200 × 30 + 280 × 30)/60 = 240.
hints: Find the cost price per kg of the mixture first.
Selling price = 1.125 × cost price.
₹240 is exactly midway between ₹200 and ₹280.

title: Republic Day to Independence Day
statement:
In 2027, Republic Day (26 January) falls on a Tuesday.
On which day of the week does Independence Day (15 August) fall in 2027? (2027 is not a leap year.)
keySteps: Count the days from 26 January to 15 August: 5 + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 15 = 201.
Move 5 days forward from Tuesday to get Sunday.
explanation: From 26 Jan to 15 Aug there are 5 (rest of Jan) + 28 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 15 = 201 days. 201 leaves remainder 5 when divided by 7, so the day is 5 days after Tuesday, which is Sunday.
hints: Count the days between the two dates month by month.
February has 28 days in 2027.
201 days; find the remainder when divided by 7.

title: Grocer's light weight
statement:
A grocer uses a false weight that is actually 800 g whenever he claims to weigh 1 kg. He also charges 10% more than his cost price per kg.
What is his actual profit percentage?
keySteps: Let the cost price be ₹100 per kg, so 800 g costs him ₹80.
He charges the customer ₹110 for what he calls 1 kg.
explanation: With cost ₹100/kg, the 800 g he actually gives costs him ₹80, but he collects ₹110. His profit is ₹30 on ₹80, which is 37.5%.
hints: Work out what the goods he actually hands over cost him.
800 g at ₹100/kg costs ₹80.
He receives ₹110 for it.

title: Sum of consecutive products
statement: Find the value of 1×2 + 2×3 + 3×4 + … + 20×21.
keySteps: Write each term as k(k + 1) = k² + k.
Sum of k² for k = 1 to 20 is 20 × 21 × 41 ÷ 6 = 2870.
Sum of k for k = 1 to 20 is 210.
explanation: Each term is k² + k, so the sum is Σk² + Σk = 2870 + 210 = 3080. The closed form n(n + 1)(n + 2)/3 = 20 × 21 × 22 ÷ 3 = 3080 gives the same.
hints: Split k(k + 1) into two simpler sums.
Use the formulas for Σk and Σk².
Σk² up to 20 is 2870 and Σk is 210.

title: Puzzle solved by someone
statement:
Three friends — Asha, Bharat and Chitra — independently try a placement puzzle. Their chances of solving it are 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4 respectively.
What is the probability that the puzzle is solved by at least one of them? Give your answer as a decimal.
keySteps: Use the complement: P(at least one) = 1 − P(nobody solves it).
explanation: Each friend fails with probability 1/2, 2/3 and 3/4. Independence gives P(all fail) = 1/4, so the puzzle is solved with probability 1 − 1/4 = 3/4 = 0.75.
hints: 'At least one' is easier through its opposite.
Find each person's chance of failing.
Multiply the failure chances and subtract from 1.

title: Train, walker and platform
statement:
A train passes a man walking at 6 km/h in the same direction as the train in 18 seconds. The same train passes a 270 m long platform in 30 seconds.
What is the speed of the train in km/h?
keySteps: Let the train's speed be v m/s and length L; the man's speed is 6 km/h = 5/3 m/s.
Passing the man: L = 18(v − 5/3), using relative speed.
explanation: With speed v m/s, passing the man gives L = 18(v − 5/3) = 18v − 30, and passing the platform gives L + 270 = 30v. So 18v + 240 = 30v, v = 20 m/s = 72 km/h, and the train is 330 m long.
hints: Write two equations in the train's length and speed.
For the man, use the relative speed v − 5/3 m/s.
Subtract to eliminate the length.

title: Men and women on a site
statement:
12 men or 18 women can complete a construction job in 14 days.
How many days will 8 men and 16 women take to complete the same job working together?
keySteps: 12 men = 18 women, so 1 man does the work of 1.5 women.
8 men = 12 women, so the team equals 12 + 16 = 28 women.
explanation: Since 12 men match 18 women, one man equals 1.5 women and 8 men equal 12 women. The team is worth 28 women. The job needs 18 × 14 = 252 woman-days, so it takes 252 ÷ 28 = 9 days.
hints: Convert men into equivalent women.
8 men are worth 12 women.
Total work is 252 woman-days; divide by 28.

title: When daughter catches up
statement:
Lakshmi is now 3 times as old as her daughter. When the daughter becomes as old as Lakshmi is now, the sum of their ages will be 112.
How old is the daughter now?
keySteps: Let the daughter be d, so Lakshmi is 3d and the age gap is 2d.
explanation: With daughter d and Lakshmi 3d, the gap is 2d. In 2d years the daughter is 3d and Lakshmi 5d, so 8d = 112 and d = 14. Check: now 14 and 42; in 28 years 42 and 70, which add to 112.
hints: The age difference never changes.
How many years until the daughter is 3d?
Write both future ages in terms of d and add them.

title: Smartphones sold in India
statement:
India has about 140 crore people. Assume roughly 60 crore of them use a smartphone and people replace their phone about once every 3–4 years.
Roughly how many smartphones are sold in India in a year?
keySteps: Start from the user base: about 60 crore smartphone users.
Each phone is replaced every 3–4 years, so yearly sales ≈ users ÷ replacement cycle.
60 ÷ 4 = 15 crore and 60 ÷ 3 = 20 crore, so the estimate lies in 10–20 crore.
explanation: If 60 crore people replace phones every 3–4 years, about 60/4 = 15 to 60/3 = 20 crore phones must be sold each year (ignoring first-time buyers, which only nudges it slightly). That falls in the 10–20 crore range, close to the real figure of roughly 15 crore a year.
hints: Yearly sales come mostly from replacements.
Divide the number of users by the replacement period.
60 crore ÷ 3 to 4 years.
